page.layout: One text column, with a narrow right margin holding one note. Running head "NOTÆ." at top, centred, page number 203 at top right. Signature "Dd 3" and catchword "rentia," at the foot.

main_text.p: الوضيع والشريف وعجالس الدهاقين والدارعين وبواكلهم ويقول انا لواحد منكم فلا قوام للدنيا الا بالعمارة التي تجري علي ايديكم وقوام العمارة بالملك لا غني لاحدهما عن الاخر [?] وعن كاخو بن ملا ديمن [?] Descendebat Rex de throno regio, & vestes albas induebat, amotóque velo ac depositio fastu regio, res hominum curabat, permissó cuilibet (sive tenuioris sive nobilioris fortis hominibus) ut cum liberè alloqueretur; quin & cum villicis & Agricolis considebat, unáque cum eis vescebatur, dicens, Ego anus sum è vobis, neque consistere potest mundus nisi cultura, quae operâ vestrâ peragitur; cultura autem ut subsistat {*}seu Regi. regno debet; neque alterum eorum sine altero consistere potest; adeo ut nos quasi fratres individui simus. Fuit hoc festum die جرم روز Jorm ruz, qui primus erat Jorm mah, sive alias ماہ ( ی Di Mah, teste Al-Kazwinio. Tum ergo demum firma sunt haec duo, regnum scil. & populi נ ד ֹ ע, cùm se invicem mutuis operis sustentant: quòd cùm innumeris penè aliorum Scriptorum, tum non paucis Scripturae sanctae testimoniis confirmatur, inter quae, si eam quam sumunt sibi, non solùm Rabbini, sed & Christiani doctores, textum Hebraicum saepe ex Arabismo explicandi libertatem, hic nobis indulgere liceat, forsan & non male illud censebitur, quod Proverbiorum, c.XXX, v. 31, occurrit, ubi inter ea quae optimi sunt incessûs, numeratur מלך אלקום עמו quae verba fictionem אלקום ex Arabum dialecto mutuatam putemus, ut fit idem quod القوم sonabunt, Rex cum quo populus est, vel quem sequitur populus suus. page.notes: Arabic and Persian lines at the top of the page are only partly legible; doubtful words are marked [?]. The Hebrew after "& populi" is printed as a Hebrew word with diacritics, read here as an approximation and should be checked. The Hebrew "מלך אלקום עמו" and "אלקום" are also uncertain in their vowel points. Italic/roman boundaries in the Latin are approximate. The catchword "rentia," is read as printed and may be a damaged "tentia,". The Latin "anus" is read as printed (possibly for "unus"). The margin note "* seu Regi." stands at the right, beside the line containing "regno debet".
